title: (No AI) Meta delays new business terms after publisher pushback on AI scraping
author: Emma Roth
content:
![Image of Meta’s wordmark on a red background.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/23951350/STK043_VRG_Illo_N_Barclay_6_Meta.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Meta is delaying the enforcement of its new business terms after publishers raised concerns that they could allow the company to scrape news sites for AI training, as [reported earlier by _Fast Company_](https://www.fastcompany.com/91628981/meta-quietly-delays-controversial-update-that-critics-say-will-allow-website-scraping). In a statement to _The Verge_, Meta spokesperson Daniel Roberts says the terms will go into effect on November 20th "to allow more time for us to explain to our partners and stakeholders what's changing and what's not."

The [business terms](https://www.facebook.com/legal/commercial_terms), which were originally supposed to go into effect on October 30th, [appeared to give Meta](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1012846/meta-business-terms-scrape-news-publishers) permission to freely scrape the new sites that use its platforms, while using the material for AI training. title: (No AI) Retro gaming is being overrun with AI
author: Andrew Webster
content:
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/01/STK465_VIDEO_GAMES_EMULATOR__CVirginia_D.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Retro video games are everywhere lately - especially in places where they aren't supposed to be. [_Halo_ in a web browser](https://www.theverge.com/games/1004952/open-halo-ce-web), [_Wind Waker_ on the iPhone](https://www.theverge.com/games/1005911/this-zelda-wind-waker-recomp-is-making-me-question-my-commitment-to-authenticity), [_Super Smash Bros._ in mixed reality](https://www.theverge.com/games/1015804/smash-bros-in-your-living-room-xelee-mixed-reality-quest-3-port). Over the past month or so, these kinds of unexpected projects have gone viral with incredible frequency thanks to new AI tools, as hobbyists take apart games and then rebuild them for new platforms. But while AI has supercharged the pace of these ports, it's also tearing apart tight-knit communities dedicated to preserving games.
